prompt: Water flows into a tank at a rate $R(t)$ liters per minute. Measurements: $R(0) = 10$, $R(3) = 14$, $R(6) = 18$, $R(10) = 20$, $R(12) = 16$. Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals given by the table to estimate the total water, in liters, that entered the tank from $t = 0$ to $t = 12$.
hint: The subintervals are not equal: their widths are $3, 3, 4, 2$. Compute each trapezoid separately with its own width.

hints.text: The subintervals are not equal: their widths are $3, 3, 4, 2$. Compute each trapezoid separately with its own width.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with the first strip: width $3$, parallel sides $10$ and $14$. Its area is $3 \cdot \frac{10 + 14}{2} = 36$ liters.
The next strips are $3 \cdot \frac{14 + 18}{2}$, $4 \cdot \frac{18 + 20}{2}$ and $2 \cdot \frac{20 + 16}{2}$. Work these out and add all four strips.
The four strips add to $36 + 48 + 76 + 36 = 196$ liters.

explanation: Rate times time gives volume, so the total water is $\int_0^{12} R(t) \, dt$, approximated by trapezoids.
Each strip is its width times the average of its two rates. On $[0, 3]$: $3 \cdot 12 = 36$. On $[3, 6]$: $3 \cdot 16 = 48$. On $[6, 10]$: $4 \cdot 19 = 76$. On $[10, 12]$: $2 \cdot 18 = 36$.
The total is about $36 + 48 + 76 + 36 = 196$ liters. The uneven widths are the trap: the shortcut formula $\frac{\Delta x}{2}(y_0 + 2y_1 + \dots)$ only works when all widths match.

alternativeExplanations.title: Average rate on each stretch
steps: A trapezoid is the same as assuming the rate was the AVERAGE of its two endpoint readings for the whole stretch.
